walkability

Quantify, diagnose, and map 10-minute pedestrian reach across urban street networks at native CPU speed.

walkability computes the reachable walkable network length within a 10-minute walk (~750 m at 4.5 km/h) for every junction in a city. Designed for urban planners and researchers, it solves two major bottlenecks in pedestrian analytics: slow routing over massive street graphs and geometric digitization biases, using a multi-threaded Rust kernel with exact partial-edge credits.


Reachable network length in Cusco. Yellow highlights dense, highly permeable pedestrian districts (Historic Center); dark purple marks fragmented outskirts and steep hillsides.

Quickstart

Installation

Install the development version from GitHub:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("PaulESantos/walkability")

Reproducible Minimal Example 

library(walkability)
library(sf)

# 1. Create a minimal 2x2 street grid (100 m spacing)
lines <- st_sfc(
  st_linestring(rbind(c(0, 0), c(100, 0))),
  st_linestring(rbind(c(100, 0), c(100, 100))),
  st_linestring(rbind(c(100, 100), c(0, 100))),
  st_linestring(rbind(c(0, 100), c(0, 0))),
  crs = 32722
)
streets <- st_as_sf(data.frame(id = 1:4), geometry = lines)

# 2. Build graph network & compute 10-minute pedestrian reach (Rust)
net   <- walk_build_network(streets, walk_speed_kmh = 4.5, verbose = FALSE)
reach <- walk_compute_reach(net, cutoff_s = 600.0, verbose = FALSE)

# 3. View results
reach
── Walkability Reachable Network Length ─────────────────────────────
v Isochrone Budget: 10.0 minutes (~750 m at 4.5 km/h)
v Evaluated Nodes: 4
* Average Reach: 0.40 km
* Highest Reach: 0.40 km
* Lowest Reach: 0.40 km
* 5th-95th percentile: 0.4 - 0.4 km

Key Capabilities

  • Non-destructive Topological Diagnosis: walk_diagnose_network() inspects user street files, flags isolated islands, and locates near-miss undershoots without mutating geometries.
  • Controlled Geometric Repair: walk_build_network() empowers users to choose whether to planarize crossings and snap dangling endpoints at specified tolerances.
  • Exact Partial-Edge Dijkstra in Rust: walk_compute_reach() computes exact fractional contributions for boundary edges across all CPU cores with zero heap reallocations.
  • Publication-Ready Maps: walk_plot_reach() renders clean ggplot2 visualizations with 2nd–98th percentile scaling and ascending layer stacking.
  • Route Directness & Circuity: walk_compute_circuity() evaluates detour ratios between network shortest paths and Euclidean distance.

Scope & Limitations

  • Modeled speed: Assumes a design walking speed of 4.5 km/h (1.25 m/s). It measures structural street connectivity, not observed GPS pedestrian speeds.
  • Footway availability: All non-motorway and non-trunk roads are modeled as walkable unless tagged as closed to pedestrians.
  • Planar topology: Grade-separated intersections (overpasses) are treated as planar unless explicit elevation tags exist.

Read the complete Methodology and Model Assumptions guide for details.

Documentation & Vignettes

  • Guía de Inicio Rápido: Complete step-by-step workflow with user-provided datasets, network repair, and diagnostic plots.
  • Metodología, Algoritmo Dijkstra en Rust y Supuestos: Mathematical derivation of the partial-edge rule, CSR representation, and 11 modeling limitations.
  • Resultados de Referencia en Ciudades: Benchmark findings and verified network statistics for Cusco, Arequipa, and Lima.
